text:
zoe: hi all, day 2 q: i'm running a local stack with docker-compose (3 containers hitting the API) and i'm getting sandbox 429s. whats the recommended pattern so each service can call the API without leaking a hosted key?
marc: welcome! :wave: for local multi-service dev use sandbox keys per-developer. avoid using the prod/hosted key in compose files. store keys in your machine's keyring or a .env that's gitignored.
zoe: right, but i need each container to make independent calls. copying the same sandbox key across containers still leads to contention/429s. any workarounds?
infra: two options we commonly use: 1) local proxy mux that serializes requests (rw-local-proxy) so you have a single token upstream but prevent parallel bursts, or 2) mint short-lived per-container tokens from the ephemeral token service and inject them into containers at startup.
zoe: rw-local-proxy? where's that and is it supported?
marc: it's a tiny tool we maintain in dev-tools. It forwards requests and applies simple concurrency limits + token rotation. Not production, but great for demos. Link: https://internal.redwood.devex/tools/rw-local-proxy
sara: if you go ephemeral tokens route, request scope 'dev:api-call' and TTL 30m. Use the service to mint tokens for each container on compose up. Example: docker-entrypoint.sh calls curl to /internal/ephemeral and writes to /run/secrets/rw_key.
devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood.devex/keys-and-quotas 1 Temporary/local patterns section covers local proxy, ephemeral tokens, and suggested concurrency defaults for sandbox. Also: account limits endpoint: GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/limits.
zoe: nice. any quick compose snippet for rw-local-proxy?
infra: small compose pattern:
```yaml
services:
  proxy:
    image: internal/rw-local-proxy:latest
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    environment:
      - RW_UPSTREAM=https://api.redwood.ai
      - RW_KEY=$RW_SANDBOX_KEY
  app:
    build: .
    environment:
      - API_BASE=http://proxy:8080
```
It routes all app traffic through proxy so you only consume one token against the sandbox and avoid per-container bursts.
zoe: for our near-term demo (10 concurrent streams) the proxy sounds limiting. can we get a temporary hosted dev key for the demo window?
devex-bot: yes, request a short-lived hosted dev key via https://internal.redwood.devex/requests/keys. Include team, demo time window, expected concurrent streams, and whether it's streaming. Turnaround usually 24-48h; ping #devex for expedite.
zoe: perfect. i'll try proxy for day-to-day dev and open a temporary hosted key request for the demo. thanks y'all :pray:
